name: French Fuchsia
lede: French Fuchsia is a vivid pink-purple named for France and the flower-color fuchsia, with no painting in our archive close enough to count.

sections.title: A place word on a flower color
sections.body: French Fuchsia pairs the place word "French" with fuchsia, a vivid pink-purple [1]. Wikipedia's color list credits the French site Pourpre.com as its source for this exact name; who first paired "French" with fuchsia, or why, is not documented in our data [1]. Its nearest named look-alikes are [[deep-pink]], [[barbie-pink]] and [[rose]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive shows this color covering at least one percent of its canvas, within CIEDE2000 4 of it, as photographed [2]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole: a vivid, modern pink-purple like this one is simply rare among historical pigments [2]. Among our French-named siblings, [[french-raspberry]] and [[french-sky-blue]] follow the same pattern: a place word in front of an existing color word, with Pourpre.com as the traced source and no painting match of note [2].
